name_en: Sanga Yaki — grilled namerou from Boso's fishing villages
summary_ja: なめろうをホタテやアワビの貝殻に詰め、鉄板や網で焼いた一品。山仕事に出る漁師がなめろうを貝殻に入れて持参し、山小屋で焼いて食べたことに由来すると伝わり、千葉の方言で「家」を「が」と呼ぶことから名がついたという。
summary_en: Namerou is packed into a scallop or abalone shell and grilled — said to come from fishermen who carried it in the shell up into the hills for woodcutting work and grilled it there, the local dialect word for "house," ga, giving the dish its name.
source_title: さんが焼き 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
